name: DWP — Income-related benefits: estimates of take-up, FYE 2024

model.name: Policy Simulation Model (PSM)
model.method: Static microsimulation on the Family Resources Survey combined with DWP and Local Authority administrative data. Recipient caseloads come from admin data; entitled non-recipients are simulated from the FRS, with admin-data linkage identifying recipients in the survey. Caseload take-up = recipients / (recipients + entitled non-recipients); expenditure take-up analogous in amounts. Ranges are 95% confidence intervals (sampling error only).
model.method_basis: Guidance sheet in the published ODS tables; background information and methodology page

period: FYE 2010 and FYE 2013 to FYE 2024 (no FYE 2011/2012 by design; FYE 2021 suppressed for COVID data-quality reasons)
geographies: Great Britain only, private households; DWP publishes no subnational take-up breakdowns
coverage_note: Working-age income-related benefit take-up is no longer published; since UC rollout the publication covers pension-age benefits (Pension Credit, Housing Benefit for pensioners) only. Savings Credit breakdowns end after FYE 2020 (population too small to estimate).
vintage_note: FYE 2024 release introduces improved admin-data-to-FRS linking and calibration-based survey weighting for entitled non-recipient estimation; methodological refinements also apply from FYE 2017. Cross-year comparisons should be treated with caution across those breaks.
diagnosis_upstream: PSM is closed-source; divergence diagnoses classified as external-model issues become a comparison memo, not an upstream PR.
